## What this was lab about

: Briefly summarize what this lab was about and what you did at a high level.
To start we had to create a website with a survey and track the analytics on the website and the data on the survey. After collecting that data, we converted the data into files and started to analyze them. This lab involved analyzing two datasets: data_analytics.csv (Google Analytics data) and data_survey.csv (survey responses). We used Python with the pandas and matplotlib libraries to load, explore, and visualize these datasets to understand website usage patterns and classmate preferences.

## Methods

: Briefly talk about the methods you used to gather the data and any specific functions that helped reveal the patterns.
We used google analytics to collect the data of our website and google forms for the survey data. After that, Data was gathered from Google Analytics (for website usage) and a survey (for classmate preferences). The pandas library was used to read CSV files into DataFrames (dfa and dfs) using pd.read_csv(). Data exploration and pattern revelation were primarily done using matplotlib.pyplot to create bar charts. Specifically, dfa['Views'] was plotted against dfa['Page path and screen class'] to visualize website views, and dfs['What is your favorite sport?'].value_counts().plot(kind='bar') was used to show the distribution of favorite sports from the survey.

I found that my classmates top sports are football and ultimate frisbee. I also discovered that the two top favorite colors in the class are orange and yellow.

## Discussion

: Briefly mention how data gathering can help you answer specific questions.
Data gathering, through methods like surveys and web analytics, is crucial for answering specific questions about user behavior, preferences, and the effectiveness of online content. For example, by collecting survey data, we can understand demographic interests, and by collecting analytics data, we can identify popular content or areas needing improvement.

## Methods

Building on this analysis, future explorations could involve correlating the survey responses with the analytics data if a common identifier or time reference were available. For example, if the survey included questions about how often respondents visit the website, we could analyze if there's a relationship between stated preferences and actual site usage patterns. Another direction could be to analyze the 'Average engagement time per active user' from the dfa to understand user stickiness on different pages, or to perform more detailed text analysis on open-ended survey responses if they were available.
